title.narrative: Improve access to lifesaving preventive and curative nutrition specific intervention for girls and boys aged 6-59 months and PLWs in Rural Damascus

description.narrative: ltpgtIn 2023, Rural Damascus (RD) governorate is witnessing an alarming rise in wasting and stunting among children under five, driven by inadequate diets for this age group, The prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) has surged doubled in the past five years, escalating from 2.6 per cent in 2019 to 5.3 per cent in 2023 across Rural Damascus governorate (SMART,2023). with 2,386 children urgently requiring life-saving treatment for Acute Malnutrition in the targeted areas (Qudsiya and Al Qutayfah). Of this group, 317 children grapple with severe wasting, presenting a significantly heightened risk of mortality. Stunting rates have consistently risen across RD governorate from 15.6 per cent in 2019 to 19.6 per cent in 2023. Furthermore, extreme poverty affected more than 1 in 4 Syrians, while it had been virtually nonexistent in 2009. This situation has weakened the ability of caregivers to provide nutritious diets to the most vulnerable children thus increasing their risk to malnutrition and death. Consequently, nearly 7 out of 10 children aged 6 to 23 months live in child food poverty meaning that they are fed fewer than the recommended 5 out of 8 food groups in a day to stand a chance of attaining optimal growth and development.ltbrgtAKHS-S has a unique advantage in direct implementation, being the sole SCO nationwide capable of direct collaboration with the Ministry of Health (MOH). As an INGO registered with MOFA and having a signed MoU with MOH, AKHS-S operates independently from the SARC, enabling direct work with District Health Offices (DOHs). This allows for prompt project execution and efficient fund utilization.lt/pgtltpgtAKHS-S can effectively implement high-impact projects with minimal funding due to their partnership with MoH, AKHS-S has an ongoing agreement MoU with the MOH to enhance access to primary health care and nutrition services for vulnerable girls, boys, and women of childbearing age across the country of Syria. To complement existing AKH_S-supported services and ensure that vulnerable children and pregnant or lactating women have access to the comprehensive preventive and curative specific nutrition interventions.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address the vulnerability of children aged 6-59 months and PLWs at high risk of malnutrition in (Qudsiya and Al Qutayfah, AKHS-S will support operation of four Nutrition response team in partnership with DoH- RD to provide the full package of preventive and curative specific nutrition interventions targeting 47,002 individuals (15,516 children aged 6-59 months, and 31,485 PLWs)ltbrgtThe proposed project is in line with Nutrition sector Humanitarian response plan 2023-2024 sector objective1) Improved access and quality to lifesaving preventive nutrition specific and sensitive interventions for children (girls and boys) under five years of age, pregnant and lactating women and Strategic objective 2) Improved access and quality to lifesaving curative nutrition interventions for children (girls and boys) under five years of age, pregnant and lactating women.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRegarding to Gender and Age Marker (GAM), the project considered the equity in delivering all activities and assistance between all beneficiaries gender in project' design and implementation phases. The GAM code for this project is /4/ (Reference: H5941-6917-4622).ltbrgtlt/pgt
